claims.text: The target material is a Ta-based BCC refractory high-entropy alloy such as MoNbTaW in a disordered solid-solution state.
MoNbTaW-type refractory BCC alloys can exhibit a significant energetic driving force for chemical short-range order.
Short-range-order effects remain significant near the melting point of the Ta-based alloy.
Full ab initio thermodynamic integration is computationally infeasible under the stated resource constraints.
An MLP-based thermodynamic-perturbation or linear-response scheme can replace full phase-space thermodynamic integration for this alloy.
Training the MLP on configurations spanning chemical SRO and local lattice distortion will improve its suitability for free-energy perturbation.
Validation against first-principles SRO energetics is more appropriate than validation only against lattice constants.
Chemical SRO and local lattice distortion are the structural mediators controlling the accuracy of the proposed free-energy calculation.
Atomic-size mismatch induces local lattice distortion in the multicomponent BCC lattice.
A machine-learning interatomic potential can model MoNbTaW over a wide temperature range while resolving effects associated with SRO.
The proposed MLP will capture the complex energy landscapes of both the liquid and solid by learning nonlinear dependence on local atomic environments.
Capturing local environments will allow perturbative estimation of solid-liquid free-energy differences without sampling the full phase space.
Standard EAM potentials fail in multicomponent systems because they cannot capture the relevant many-body interactions and SRO energetics.
The SRO-aware MLP perturbation scheme will predict melting temperatures and free-energy differences within 5% of high-accuracy ab initio benchmarks.
CALPHAD trends can serve as an alternative accuracy reference when direct ab initio benchmarks are unavailable.
The proposed method will reduce computational time by orders of magnitude relative to full thermodynamic integration.
Standard EAM predictions will deviate by more than 10% because of missing SRO effects.
The method may fail when long-range ordering or complex phase transformations are absent from the training set.
Omitting representative liquid structures or high-temperature SRO configurations from the training set may bias the perturbative free-energy results.
Rare-event undersampling and failure of perturbation-series convergence in highly disordered liquids are possible failure modes of TOR-TILD-like approaches in multicomponent spaces.
